evidence.excerpt:
The structural analysis in Figure 5 and Figure 6 is computed on 85 solved Tents instances (3 traces × 3 instances per size
per model; 20/35/30 for DeepSeek/Kimi/Qwen3), balanced across sizes (24/20/21/20 for 4 × 4 through 7 × 7).

facts.description: 失败对照的匹配/排除规则及相关系数区间明确，bootstrap在85实例上5000次重采样。

evidence.excerpt:
Efficiency below the solved subset. We additionally compare structural metrics on incorrect Tents traces against correct
traces at matched puzzle sizes. We exclude failed generations (truncated or aborted runs producing fewer than ∼ 1k
completion tokens and no extractable reasoning), which reflect infrastructure failures rather than flawed reasoning. On the
remaining failed traces (n = 10 incorrect vs. 35 matched correct, sizes 5 × 5–7 × 7, three models; Table 10), reasoning-flow
efficiency is 57% lower, claim accuracy is ∼ 14% lower, and the first error appears ∼ 51% earlier. Failed traces are also larger
(+52% nodes), wider (+73%), and higher-entropy, and devote a smaller fraction of the graph to the solution, indicating that
failing models reason more diffusely from early on rather than making isolated late mistakes. This analysis is limited to
Tents; a broader study across puzzle families is left to future work.
